title: UNEP Mountains ADAPT Small Grants 2026: Apply for Up to USD 30,000 to Strengthen Climate Resilience in East African Mountain Communities.
summary: Climate change continues to pose significant threats to mountain ecosystems and the millions of people who depend on them for water, agriculture, biodiversity, and sustainable livelihoods. To help local communities respond to these growing challenges, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) has officially opened the first Call for Proposals under the Mountains ADAPT Small Grants Project for 2026. This funding opportunity provides grants of up to USD 30,000 to eligible community-based organizations working in mountain regions across the East African Community (EAC). Through these grants, UNEP aims to empower local organizations to design and implement ecosystem-based adaptation initiatives that protect natural resources, strengthen climate resilience, and improve community livelihoods. Beyond financial support, selected organizations will also receive technical assistance, capacity development, and implementation training to ensure their projects achieve sustainable and measurable impacts. Applications are now open and must be submitted no later than 15 September 2026 at 11:59 PM East African Time (EAT). About the UNEP Mountains ADAPT Small Grants Project The Mountains ADAPT initiative is a UNEP-led project that promotes climate resilience in mountain regions through ecosystem-based adaptation and nature-based solutions. Mountain ecosystems are among the most vulnerable environments affected by climate change, making local adaptation initiatives increasingly important. The project recognizes that local organizations possess valuable knowledge of their communities and landscapes. By investing directly in community-led solutions, UNEP seeks to strengthen environmental conservation while improving the social and economic wellbeing of mountain populations. The first call for proposals focuses specifically on countries within the East African Community (EAC), where mountain communities are experiencing increasing climate-related risks such as: Drought Flooding Soil erosion Water scarcity Biodiversity loss Declining agricultural productivity Landslides Extreme weather events The project supports innovative solutions that not only address these challenges but also create long-term environmental and economic resilience. Grant Value Successful organizations may receive funding of up to: USD 30,000 There is no officially defined minimum funding amount. Applicants are encouraged to request a realistic budget that adequately supports meaningful project implementation. In addition to financial support, successful organizations will receive: Capacity development Technical guidance Project implementation training Institutional strengthening Monitoring and evaluation support Number of Projects to be Funded During this first funding round, UNEP plans to support: Up to 15 community-led projects across the East African Community. Objectives of the Small Grants Programme The Mountains ADAPT Small Grants Programme seeks to: Strengthen climate resilience in mountain communities. Promote ecosystem-based adaptation. Support community-driven environmental conservation. Protect mountain ecosystems. Improve local livelihoods. Encourage gender-inclusive climate action. Increase community ownership of adaptation projects. Enhance sustainable management of natural resources. Promote innovative nature-based solutions. Types of Projects That Can Be Funded Applicants are encouraged to develop practical, community-led projects that address local climate challenges through ecosystem-based adaptation. Examples of eligible interventions include: Ecosystem Restoration Projects may include: Forest restoration Indigenous tree planting Watershed rehabilitation Riverbank restoration Wetland conservation Soil restoration Water Management Potential activities include: Rainwater harvesting Spring protection Water conservation Community water infrastructure Sustainable watershed management Climate-Smart Agriculture Projects may support: Sustainable farming Agroforestry Improved irrigation Soil conservation Drought-resilient farming Sustainable food production Disaster Risk Reduction Organizations may propose activities such as: Community disaster preparedness Early warning systems Landslide prevention Flood mitigation Risk awareness campaigns Sustainable Livelihoods Projects may also include: Income diversification Green enterprises Community environmental businesses Sustainable natural resource management What Makes a Strong Proposal? UNEP encourages organizations to submit projects that: Respond to clearly identified climate risks. Demonstrate strong community ownership. Use ecosystem-based adaptation approaches. Integrate gender equality considerations. Promote youth participation where possible. Deliver measurable environmental and social benefits. Can be sustained beyond the grant period. Show innovation and potential for scaling up. What the Application Must Include Organizations are required to provide comprehensive information during the application process. 1. Organizational Information Applicants should provide: Organization name Registration details Registration number Organizational experience Previous projects Experience in mountain regions 2. Climate Challenge Applicants must explain: The climate risks affecting the community. Why the problem is significant. Visual evidence demonstrating the challenge. 3. Proposed Solution Organizations should describe: The planned intervention. How it addresses climate change. Ecosystem-based adaptation methods. Nature-based solutions. Gender-responsive approaches. Expected environmental outcomes. 4. Beneficiaries Applicants should identify: Target communities. Expected beneficiaries. Community participation. Long-term benefits. 5. Required Attachments Applicants must upload: Organization registration certificate. National ID or passport of the legal representative. Evidence of previous project experience. Who Can Apply? Eligible applicants include registered community organizations operating within mountain regions of eligible East African Community countries. Organizations should have demonstrated experience serving mountain communities and implementing environmental or climate-related initiatives. Eligible applicants include: Community-based organizations Grassroots organizations Civil society organizations Youth organizations Women-led organizations Registered NGOs Individuals are not eligible to apply. APPLY HERE. Countries Eligible for the Grant Organizations must be based in one of the following countries: Burundi Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) Kenya Rwanda Somalia South Sudan Tanzania Uganda Required Organizational Experience Applicants should demonstrate: Previous work with mountain communities. Capacity to manage community projects. Knowledge of local environmental challenges. Experience implementing adaptation or environmental initiatives. Organizations do not need prior experience managing international donor funding. Required Documents Applicants must submit: Official registration certificate. National ID or passport of the legal representative. If selected, organizations must also provide: Official organizational bank account details. Eligible Project Costs Grant funding may be used for: Staff salaries Technical experts Equipment Project materials Community training Capacity-building activities Administrative costs Operational expenses Project implementation costs Funding Restrictions The grant cannot be used for: Direct salaries or allowances to government officials. Payments that fall outside the approved project scope. Government participation is encouraged through in-kind support or co-financing rather than direct grant payments. Is Co-Funding Required? No. Organizations are not required to secure co-funding. However, proposals with existing or anticipated financial support from municipalities or development partners may receive additional consideration during evaluation. Application Evaluation Process Applications will undergo several stages. Stage 1: Eligibility Screening Applications will first be reviewed to ensure: Eligibility requirements are met. Required documents are submitted. Application forms are complete. Stage 2: Technical Evaluation Eligible proposals will then be assessed by the Selection Committee using an official evaluation matrix. Key assessment criteria include: Relevance to climate challenges Technical feasibility Community participation Innovation Gender inclusion Youth inclusion Sustainability Environmental safeguards Potential for scaling up Stage 3: Final Selection Regional Selection Committees will select up to 15 successful projects. Click HERE for more information on UNEP Mountains ADAPT Small Grants 2026. What Happens After Selection? Successful organizations will: Develop a detailed implementation plan. Prepare milestones and timelines. Receive organizational capacity assessments. Participate in technical training. Receive tailored implementation support. Begin project implementation. Reporting Requirements Successful organizations must submit: Mid-Term Report Including: Project progress Financial expenditure Supporting documentation Final Report Including: Final achievements Financial reporting Photos Videos Project evidence Some projects may also be selected for field monitoring visits. Project Timeline Key milestones include: Application deadline: 15 September 2026 (11:59 PM EAT) Notification of selected organizations: Third Quarter of 2026 Project implementation begins: Fourth Quarter of 2026 Grant implementation period: 12 months Languages Accepted Applications may be submitted in: English French Kiswahili How to Apply Interested organizations should: Complete the official online application form. Upload all required supporting documents. Submit the proposal before the deadline. Await eligibility screening. Respond to any requests for additional information if contacted. Wait for the regional selection process and notification. Need Assistance? Organizations requiring technical support or clarification during the application process may contact the UNEP Mountains ADAPT project team via: Email: unep-mountainsadapt@un.org Why Organizations Should Apply The Mountains ADAPT Small Grants Programme offers more than funding. It provides local organizations with an opportunity to strengthen institutional capacity, implement community-led climate solutions, and contribute to long-term environmental sustainability across East Africa s mountain ecosystems. Organizations will benefit from technical guidance, increased visibility, and practical experience implementing nature-based adaptation strategies that improve resilience for vulnerable communities. For organizations already working with mountain communities, this grant presents an excellent opportunity to expand their impact while contributing to regional climate adaptation goals. Conclusion The 2026 UNEP Mountains ADAPT Small Grants Programme is an important funding opportunity for community-based organizations dedicated to protecting mountain ecosystems and improving climate resilience across the East African Community. With grants of up to USD 30,000, comprehensive technical support, and a strong emphasis on ecosystem-based adaptation, the programme empowers local organizations to lead transformative environmental initiatives that benefit both people and nature. Eligible organizations are encouraged to prepare high-quality proposals that demonstrate strong community engagement, innovative climate solutions, and sustainable environmental outcomes. Interested applicants should ensure they submit all required documents before the 15 September 2026 deadline to be considered for this competitive funding opportunity. For more OFY Grant opportunities VISIT HERE. title: MIT School Access and Quality Fellowship 2026–2027: One-Year Fellowship for Education Leaders Advancing Equitable School Access and AI-Driven Education Policy
summary: Applications are now open for the MIT School Access and Quality (SAQ) Fellowship 2026–2027 , a prestigious one-year professional development programme designed for education leaders committed to improving educational equity through more effective school enrollment and school performance policies. Hosted by Blueprint Labs at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) , the fellowship brings together leaders from public school districts, state education agencies, charter management organizations, and nonprofit organizations to learn from leading researchers, policy experts, and fellow practitioners. Through a combination of in-person and virtual programming, participants develop the knowledge, practical skills, and professional network needed to build more equitable, transparent, and efficient education systems. As technology and Artificial Intelligence (AI) increasingly influence education policy and school enrollment systems, the fellowship also explores how these emerging tools can be used responsibly to improve educational equity while ensuring that all students and families have fair access to high-quality schools. Applications are open until 24 August 2026 at 5:00 PM ET . About the MIT School Access and Quality (SAQ) Fellowship The MIT School Access and Quality Fellowship is an intensive leadership programme focused on helping education professionals strengthen school enrollment systems and improve school performance policies. The fellowship recognizes that equitable enrollment practices and fair school performance measures are essential for ensuring that every child—regardless of background, geography, race, or socioeconomic status—has access to quality education. Rather than offering purely theoretical instruction, the fellowship combines research, policy discussions, peer learning, and practical problem-solving to help participants implement evidence-based solutions within their own organizations and communities. Throughout the year, Fellows engage directly with: MIT researchers Education policy experts Enrollment specialists School system leaders Fellow practitioners from across the United States The programme creates a collaborative learning environment where participants share experiences, exchange ideas, and develop practical strategies to improve educational outcomes. Why the School Access and Quality Fellowship Matters Across the United States, education systems are experiencing significant challenges. These include: Declining student enrollment Persistent educational inequities Unequal access to high-performing schools Family disengagement Inconsistent school performance measures Increasing complexity in enrollment systems Growing use of Artificial Intelligence in educational decision-making Many school districts and education organizations lack sufficient resources or evidence-based guidance to redesign enrollment systems in ways that improve fairness and educational access. The MIT SAQ Fellowship addresses these challenges by equipping education leaders with research-backed strategies, collaborative learning opportunities, and practical tools that can strengthen enrollment policies while keeping equity at the center of decision-making. Fellowship Objectives The programme aims to help education leaders build stronger, fairer, and more effective school systems. By the end of the fellowship, participants will be better prepared to: Improve educational equity Design better enrollment policies Strengthen school performance systems Build trust with families and communities Improve decision-making through research Apply Artificial Intelligence responsibly within education Collaborate across different education sectors Lead evidence-based policy reforms What Fellows Will Learn The fellowship curriculum focuses on contemporary issues affecting school access and education policy. Participants will explore topics including: 1. Improving Educational Equity Fellows learn how enrollment policies can promote: Fair school access Equal opportunities Inclusive education Better student outcomes 2. Family and Community Engagement Participants examine strategies for: Working effectively with families Building stakeholder trust Encouraging community participation Improving communication 3. Artificial Intelligence in Education A distinctive component of the fellowship is its focus on AI. Participants learn how AI can be used to: Forecast school enrollment Evaluate enrollment policies Improve education planning Support evidence-based decisions The programme also considers important questions regarding: Equity Accessibility Responsible AI Family experiences with AI-driven school choice systems 4. Data-Driven Decision Making Participants strengthen their ability to use education data to: Support students Improve school access Inform policy decisions Evaluate educational outcomes 5. Collaboration Between School Systems The fellowship explores ways to improve collaboration between: Public school districts Charter schools Education agencies Community organizations 6. Addressing Enrollment Decline Participants develop strategies for responding to: Declining student populations Resource allocation challenges School planning Equity-centered enrollment policies 7. School Performance Measurement The fellowship also examines methods for creating: More accurate school performance measures Fair accountability systems Better educational evaluation frameworks 8. Selective School Admissions Participants discuss equitable approaches to: Seat allocation Admissions policies Access to selective schools 9. User-Friendly Enrollment Systems The programme helps Fellows design enrollment systems that are: Accessible Transparent Easy for families to navigate Inclusive for diverse communities Fellowship Programming The SAQ Fellowship combines in-person experiences with virtual learning throughout the year. In-Person Programming Two-Day Kickoff at MIT The fellowship begins with a two-day event hosted at MIT. Participants: Meet fellow cohort members Explore key education policy issues Build relationships Begin collaborative learning City Learning Visit Fellows also participate in a two-day immersive visit to another city where they study real-world enrollment and school performance practices. This allows participants to observe innovative education systems and learn directly from local practitioners. Virtual Programming Throughout the year, Fellows participate in a variety of online learning opportunities. Monthly Challenge Sessions Participants work together on case studies and discuss practical solutions to real enrollment and school performance challenges. Webinar Series Leading researchers and policy experts deliver presentations covering: Education policy Enrollment systems School performance Equity Artificial Intelligence Expert Office Hours Fellows receive personalized support through one-on-one meetings with enrollment specialists and research experts. Capstone Project Each Fellow completes an individual project during the programme. At the end of the fellowship, participants present their work and lessons learned to the cohort. Ongoing Virtual Community The fellowship maintains active engagement through: Monthly Newsletters Participants receive regular updates featuring: Education news Research Resources Event summaries Policy developments Online Learning Portal Current Fellows and alumni share: Resources Best practices Research Collaboration opportunities Who Can Become a Fellow? The fellowship is designed for professionals working in education leadership roles. Participants typically come from: Public school districts State education agencies Charter management organizations Nonprofit organizations Their diverse professional experiences enrich discussions and strengthen collaborative learning. Alumni Community Participation extends beyond the one-year programme. Graduates become members of an active alumni network and are encouraged to continue participating in: Events Knowledge sharing Professional collaboration Fellowship activities This lifelong network enables continued learning and partnership among education leaders. Why Focus on School Enrollment and Performance? MIT highlights several pressing challenges facing education today. These include: Nationwide declines in public school enrollment Increasing student disengagement Persistent inequities in school access Limited access to accurate school quality information Despite these challenges, enrollment systems remain one of the most powerful tools for improving educational equity. The fellowship equips participants with the research, knowledge, and practical skills needed to redesign these systems in ways that better serve students, families, and communities. Benefits of the Fellowship Participants benefit from numerous professional development opportunities, including: One-year leadership development programme Access to MIT researchers and education experts Peer learning with education leaders nationwide Two-day kickoff event at MIT Two-day city learning visit Monthly challenge sessions Webinar series Individual expert office hours Capstone project Monthly education newsletters Online collaboration platform Lifelong alumni network Practical AI and education policy training Opportunities to exchange ideas with leaders across education sectors Application Deadline Applications for the MIT School Access and Quality Fellowship are currently open. Application Deadline: 24 August 2026 at 5:00 PM ET Interested applicants should submit their applications before the deadline. How to Apply Prospective applicants should complete the official online application through the MIT School Access and Quality Fellowship webpage. Applicants are encouraged to: Review the fellowship objectives. Confirm that their professional role aligns with the programme. Prepare any required application materials. Submit their application before 24 August 2026 at 5:00 PM ET . Learn more about applying APPLY HERE Frequently Asked Questions What is the Fellowship s timeline? The Fellowship starts with an in-person Kickoff event in the fall. It concludes in early summer with the City Learning Visit and a written reflection of each Fellow’s accomplishments. When and where are the events? The location of the in-person events varies by cohort. Fellows will be polled and notified of the event dates and locations in advance. Some events may be hybrid or virtual only. What are some examples of past topics? In recent cohorts, we have covered many topics, such as how to: improve equity in Fellows’ cities, use enrollment data to drive decision-making, develop more equitable and accurate school quality measures, engage the community to foster equitable enrollment, increase access to early childhood education, unify enrollment for after-school programs, improve relationships between districts and charters, address declining enrollment, and more. What if my region hasn’t yet started unified enrollment? Everyone is welcome to join. We think that the diversity in current enrollment practices is an asset to this Fellowship – Fellows can learn from one another about potential challenges and opportunities. What is the estimated time commitment as a Fellow? Fellows are expected to attend a two day Kickoff, a two-day City Learning Visit, two hour-long webinars (out of three), and monthly challenge sessions. Fellows are also expected to dedicate several hours throughout the Fellowship to completing a capstone project of their choosing and preparing a short presentation on their efforts. Fellows will also submit a summary of accomplishments upon the conclusion of the program. Who do I contact with questions? Please reach out to tgerstle@mitblueprintlabs.org with any questions. Is there any financial obligation associated with the Fellowship? There is no fee associated with the Fellowship, though Fellows (or their organizations) are expected to cover the costs of travel and lodging for both in-person events. Five travel scholarships are available based on need and merit to cover up to $1,200 in travel and lodging expenses for each event. What is the capstone project? Fellows will commit to a project of their choosing related to enrollment or school performance (e.g., implementing a new school quality measure, pursuing an enrollment policy change). Periodically, Fellows will report on their progress, culminating in a 5-minute presentation about their accomplishments at the end of the year. Source: https://blueprintlabs.mit.edu/apply-to-the-school-access-and-quality-fellowship/ Why You Should Apply The MIT School Access and Quality Fellowship offers an exceptional opportunity for education leaders seeking to improve equity in school enrollment and performance systems. Rather than focusing solely on theory, the fellowship provides practical strategies, collaborative learning experiences, and direct access to leading researchers and policy experts. Participants gain valuable insights into AI-enabled education systems, data-informed decision-making, and evidence-based policies that can improve educational opportunities for students nationwide. For professionals committed to building fairer, more inclusive education systems, this fellowship provides the knowledge, network, and leadership development needed to drive meaningful change. Visit HERE to learn more about the MIT School Access and Quality Fellowship. Conclusion The MIT School Access and Quality Fellowship 2026–2027 is an outstanding professional development opportunity for education leaders working to create more equitable school enrollment systems and improve school performance policies. Through a year-long combination of in-person events, virtual learning, expert mentorship, collaborative problem-solving, and research-informed discussions, Fellows develop practical skills that can transform educational access and outcomes in their communities. By examining pressing challenges such as declining enrollment, school accountability, family engagement, and the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence in education, the fellowship prepares participants to lead innovative and equitable reforms. Those working within public education systems, charter organizations, state education agencies, and nonprofit organizations are encouraged to apply before the 24 August 2026 at 5:00 PM ET deadline to become part of this distinguished network of education leaders. Discover more global Fellowship and Leadership Development opportunities on OFY. title: Research Assistant – U.S. Immigration Policy Program at the Migration Policy Institute (MPI): Apply for a Policy Research Career in Washington, D.C.
summary: If you are passionate about immigration policy, public policy research, legal and regulatory analysis, and evidence-based policymaking, the Migration Policy Institute (MPI) is offering an outstanding opportunity to advance your career. The organization is currently recruiting a Research Assistant to join its U.S. Immigration Policy Program in Washington, D.C. This role is ideal for early-career professionals who are eager to contribute to one of the world s leading independent think tanks focusing on migration, immigration, refugee policy, and integration. Successful applicants will work alongside renowned policy experts, researchers, and analysts while contributing to influential research that informs policymakers, stakeholders, and the public. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so interested candidates are encouraged to submit their applications as early as possible. About the Migration Policy Institute (MPI) The Migration Policy Institute (MPI) is an independent, nonpartisan think tank dedicated to improving immigration and integration policies through rigorous research, objective analysis, policy dialogue, and innovative solutions. MPI has built an international reputation for producing authoritative research on migration and immigration issues affecting governments, institutions, and communities around the world. Rather than advocating for political positions, the institute focuses on producing evidence-based research that helps policymakers make informed decisions. The organization values: Independent and objective research Policy innovation Diversity of thought Inclusive workplaces Evidence-based decision-making Professional excellence MPI is also deeply committed to creating an equitable workplace where employees from diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives are welcomed and supported. About the U.S. Immigration Policy Program The successful candidate will become part of MPI s highly respected U.S. Immigration Policy Program. This team conducts extensive research on the major immigration policy issues affecting the United States. Their work influences discussions among lawmakers, researchers, advocacy organizations, journalists, and government agencies. The program covers a broad range of immigration topics, including: Legal immigration pathways Employment and family visa systems Refugee admissions and resettlement Asylum policies Border management Immigration enforcement Immigration governance Demographic trends Characteristics of immigrant populations Federal immigration legislation Executive immigration actions Court decisions affecting immigration Regulatory developments Beyond publishing research, the program also organizes conferences, policy dialogues, stakeholder meetings, webinars, and public events that encourage informed discussion on immigration issues. About the Research Assistant Position The Research Assistant will support the institute s research, policy monitoring, analytical writing, and project management activities. This is an excellent opportunity for someone seeking long-term professional growth in policy research, immigration studies, public affairs, or legal analysis. Working closely with senior researchers, the successful candidate will help monitor rapidly changing immigration developments while contributing to publications that reach policymakers and national audiences. The role offers opportunities for increasing responsibility based on performance. Key Responsibilities The successful applicant will perform a wide variety of research, analytical, and administrative responsibilities. 1. Immigration Policy Monitoring One of the primary responsibilities involves closely following developments in U.S. immigration policy. This includes monitoring: Congressional legislation Executive actions Regulatory changes Court rulings Immigration agency guidance Federal policy announcements The Research Assistant will summarize and synthesize these developments for both internal and public-facing audiences. 2. Conduct Policy Research The position requires assisting with both qualitative and quantitative research. Responsibilities include: Conducting literature reviews Collecting policy documents Gathering statistical information Organizing research materials Identifying relevant data sources Supporting evidence-based policy analysis 3. Data Collection and Analysis The Research Assistant will help compile reliable datasets used in MPI publications. Tasks include: Cleaning datasets Verifying information Producing statistical tables Creating charts and figures Organizing research databases Ensuring data accuracy 4. Interview Support Research often involves interviewing experts and stakeholders. The Research Assistant will: Schedule interviews Participate in interviews Prepare interview summaries Draft research memoranda Organize qualitative findings Some travel may be required. 5. Writing and Publication Support The successful applicant will contribute to numerous research outputs, including: Research reports Policy briefs Background papers Commentaries Memoranda Short-form analyses Writing will be supervised by senior researchers, providing valuable mentorship and professional development. 6. Use of Artificial Intelligence MPI encourages responsible use of AI technologies in accordance with institutional policies. Research assistants may utilize approved AI tools while maintaining research integrity and quality standards. 7. Event Coordination The position also includes helping organize: Public events Private policy roundtables Webinars Research briefings Stakeholder meetings Conference calls This work will be carried out in collaboration with MPI s Communications Team. 8. Project Management Support The Research Assistant will assist with various operational activities, including: Scheduling meetings Tracking project timelines Coordinating research activities Supporting internal communications Managing documentation 9. Intern Supervision The successful candidate may assist senior staff in: Recruiting interns Supervising intern activities Providing project guidance Coordinating intern assignments 10. Fundraising Support MPI researchers also contribute to fundraising initiatives. The Research Assistant will assist by: Researching funding opportunities Drafting grant proposal sections Writing concept notes Preparing donor reports Collecting background information Required Qualifications Applicants should meet the following minimum requirements. Educational Background Candidates should possess: A Bachelor s degree with at least one year of relevant work experience. Alternatively: Candidates without a bachelor s degree who can demonstrate substantial relevant professional experience may also be considered. Research Skills Applicants should demonstrate: Strong analytical thinking Excellent research abilities Experience supporting original research Ability to synthesize complex information Critical evaluation skills Writing Skills Excellent written English is essential. Applicants should be capable of producing: Clear policy writing Research summaries Professional reports Analytical memoranda Immigration Policy Knowledge Candidates should already possess knowledge in at least two areas such as: Visa pathways Immigration enforcement Border management Refugee resettlement Asylum policy Legal Research Applicants should either have experience with legal research or demonstrate willingness to learn. This includes reviewing: Federal laws Regulations Court decisions Policy guidance Administrative documents Professional Competencies Successful applicants should also demonstrate: High attention to detail Strong organizational skills Excellent time management Ability to prioritize competing assignments Initiative and self-motivation Teamwork and collaboration Effective communication skills Commitment to factual accuracy Preferred Qualifications Although not mandatory, the following qualifications will strengthen an application: Foreign language proficiency Knowledge of immigration law Advanced Excel skills Experience with Stata Experience using statistical software Quantitative data analysis expertise Salary and Benefits The position offers competitive compensation. Salary Annual salary ranges from: US$52,000–US$67,000 Compensation will depend on the successful applicant s experience, qualifications, and skills. Benefits Employees receive generous benefits, including: Health insurance Retirement benefits Professional development opportunities Collaborative work environment Career advancement opportunities Work Location This is a Washington, D.C.-based position . Employees are expected to work: At least three days per week in the office . How to Apply Interested applicants should prepare the following application materials: Cover letter Resume One unedited, sole-authored writing sample Applications should be submitted via email to: hr@migrationpolicy.org When applying: Label each file using your last name. Use Research Assistant, U.S. Program as the email subject line. Include a brief statement indicating how you learned about the vacancy. Application Deadline Application Deadline: August 24 Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, meaning qualified candidates may be interviewed before the deadline. Applicants are therefore strongly encouraged to apply as early as possible. Due to the anticipated volume of applications, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Applicants are also requested not to contact MPI staff directly regarding the recruitment process. Equal Opportunity Employer The Migration Policy Institute is an Equal Opportunity Employer. MPI welcomes applications from qualified candidates regardless of: Race Ethnicity Gender Religion Sexual orientation Gender identity Physical ability The organization is committed to fostering a workplace that values diversity, equity, inclusion, and mutual respect. Why You Should Consider This Opportunity This Research Assistant position presents an exceptional opportunity for individuals seeking careers in migration policy, public policy, research, international affairs, law, or social sciences. Working at the Migration Policy Institute provides exposure to nationally significant immigration policy discussions, opportunities to collaborate with leading experts, and the chance to contribute to influential research that informs public debate and policymaking. The combination of policy research, analytical writing, event coordination, and professional mentorship makes this an outstanding entry point for aspiring policy researchers and analysts. Because applications are reviewed as they are received, interested candidates should prepare their materials promptly and submit a strong application well before the August 24 deadline. Visit HERE to learn more about the Research Assistant – U.S. Immigration Policy Program at the Migration Policy Institute. For more global Job opportunity visit OFY HERE. title: Disney Internships in the United States 2026: Gain Paid, Real-World Experience at The Walt Disney Company
summary: The Walt Disney Company is offering internship opportunities in the United States for students and emerging professionals interested in gaining practical experience within one of the world’s most recognized entertainment and media organizations. Disney Internships are designed to connect academic learning with professional experience. Successful candidates are placed in specific business areas where they can contribute to real projects, learn from experienced professionals and develop industry-relevant skills. Depending on the role, interns may contribute to television production, journalism, filmmaking, engineering, finance, accounting, marketing, technology, design, communications, legal affairs or guest experiences. Opportunities are offered across major Disney business segments, including Corporate, Disney Entertainment, Disney Experiences and ESPN. The programme is not one single internship with a common application form or deadline. Disney publishes separate vacancies throughout the year, and every position has its own responsibilities, qualifications, location, work schedule and application requirements. Interested candidates should therefore review each vacancy carefully before applying. Disney Internships in the United States About The Walt Disney Company The Walt Disney Company is a global entertainment organization known for creating films, television programmes, sports content, theme-park experiences and consumer products. Its businesses and brands reach audiences around the world through storytelling, creative production and technology. Disney’s portfolio includes businesses and brands associated with Disney Entertainment, ESPN, Disney Experiences, ABC, FX, National Geographic, Disney Branded Television and other entertainment and media operations. A Disney internship gives participants an opportunity to understand how a large international organization develops content, manages its businesses, engages audiences and delivers experiences across multiple platforms. What Are Disney Internships? Disney Internships are professional learning opportunities in which students work within a particular academic or career field. Instead of only observing an organization, interns may support actual assignments, projects and business operations under professional supervision. Depending on the placement, an intern could have an opportunity to: Contribute to television programmes and media productions Support the creation and development of films and entertainment content Assist projects designed for sports audiences Participate in communications and marketing assignments Support finance, accounting or business operations Work on engineering or technology-related projects Assist teams responsible for guest and consumer experiences Develop research, writing, analytical or creative skills The exact duties depend entirely on the position. Applicants should not assume that every Disney internship offers the same experience or follows the same selection criteria. Disney Business Segments Offering Internships Internships may be available across several parts of The Walt Disney Company. 1. Disney Corporate Corporate internships may involve departments responsible for managing and supporting Disney’s wider business operations. Potential areas can include: Finance and accounting Human resources Legal affairs Risk management Business operations Communications Data and analytics Technology Strategy and administrative support 2. Disney Entertainment Disney Entertainment opportunities may allow interns to gain exposure to television, film, streaming, news, production and content-development operations. Depending on the vacancy, interns may work with teams connected to ABC, FX, National Geographic, Disney Branded Television and other entertainment businesses. 3. Disney Experiences Disney Experiences manages businesses associated with theme parks, resorts, cruises, travel experiences and consumer products. Internship assignments may involve guest services, marketing, engineering, entertainment, operations, finance, communications or business support. 4. ESPN ESPN internships may provide experience in sports media, journalism, production, technology, marketing and related business functions. These roles can be suitable for candidates interested in combining professional skills with the sports and media industries. Available Fields of Study and Professional Disciplines Disney states that its internship disciplines are as diverse as its business units. Internship areas can include, but are not limited to: Broadcast, production and journalism Communications Costuming and entertainment Creative and graphic design Engineering Finance and accounting Sales and marketing promotions Technology Legal affairs Risk management Data and analytics Business operations Human resources The available fields change as vacancies open and close. Applicants should use the Disney Careers search function to locate opportunities related to their education, skills and professional interests. Disney Internship Locations in the United States Disney lists internship opportunities in several major American cities and business centres, including: Anaheim, California Burbank and Glendale, California Bristol, Connecticut New York, New York Orlando, Florida San Francisco, California Santa Monica, California Seattle, Washington Remote locations within the United States Other locations according to business requirements A vacancy marked “Remote, USA” should not automatically be interpreted as an internationally remote position. It generally means the work can be performed remotely within the United States, subject to the conditions stated in that particular job description. Many on-site positions require interns to arrange their own accommodation and transportation. Applicants must review the location requirements before submitting an application. Duration of Disney Internships Disney’s general internship page states that programmes commonly last between three and six months. Some assignments may be extended for up to one year. The actual duration varies by position. Individual vacancies may require candidates to be available throughout a specified semester or set of dates, such as: Spring internships Summer internships Fall internships Semester-long assignments Extended programmes lasting several months Applicants should only apply if they can remain available for the entire period stated in the vacancy. Disney also notes that existing Disney Internship, College, International or Culinary Program participants may generally work for only one consecutive year, or 12 months, across any combination of applicable internships and programmes. Are Disney Internships Paid? Disney describes its internship opportunities within a broader total-rewards framework that may include pay and other employment-related benefits. However, compensation and benefit arrangements vary by position and location. Candidates should consult the individual vacancy to confirm: Hourly pay or salary range Expected number of working hours Part-time or full-time status Eligibility for specific employee benefits Whether relocation support is available Whether accommodation is provided Applicants should not assume that Disney will cover housing, transportation, visa or relocation expenses unless the specific vacancy expressly says so. Benefits of Joining a Disney Internship Benefits vary according to the internship, business segment and location. Disney identifies potential benefits and work-related advantages such as: Hands-on professional experience Interns can apply their academic knowledge in a real workplace and understand how professional teams manage assignments, deadlines and organizational priorities. Career development Disney provides learning tools and programmes intended to support employee and cast-member development. Internship-specific programming may also help participants build professional knowledge and workplace skills. Exposure to major entertainment businesses Depending on the placement, interns may support projects connected with television, film, sports, theme parks, digital platforms or corporate operations. title: CDC Campaign and Audience Research Team Fellowship 2026 in the USA
summary: Public health communication plays a critical role in helping communities make informed decisions that improve health outcomes. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is now accepting applications for the CDC Campaign and Audience Research Team Fellowship 2026, a unique research and training opportunity for recent graduates interested in communication science, audience research, and public health messaging. Hosted by the Division of Communication Science and Services (DCSS) within the CDC’s Office of Communications, this fellowship offers participants the chance to gain practical experience in communication research while working alongside experts who develop evidence-based public health communication strategies. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, with a final deadline of September 25, 2026. About the CDC Campaign and Audience Research Team Fellowship The fellowship is designed to provide a mentored educational experience focused on communication science research and public health communication practices. Participants will engage with the CDC’s Campaign and Audience Research Team (CART), learning how communication strategies are developed, tested, and evaluated to reach diverse audiences effectively. The Division of Communication Science and Services supports public health practitioners by providing technical assistance, communication tools, training resources, and evidence-based messaging that is understandable, accessible, and actionable. Fellowship Location The fellowship will be hosted at the: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Atlanta, Georgia, United States Fellowship Benefits Selected fellows will receive: • Full-time mentored training experience at the CDC • Competitive monthly stipend (amount varies based on qualifications and experience) • Exposure to communication science research and public health campaigns • Opportunities to work with communication experts and researchers • Experience in audience research, message testing, and public health communication strategies • Potential involvement in communication activities during public health emergency responses • Professional development opportunities and collaborative learning experiences • Possibility of fellowship renewal beyond the initial one-year appointment, subject to funding and performance Learning Opportunities Through this fellowship, participants will have opportunities to: • Apply communication science techniques to public health communication projects • Participate in qualitative and quantitative communication research activities • Conduct literature reviews and audience research • Learn how communication messages are developed and tailored for specific audiences • Gain experience analyzing audience data and evaluating communication effectiveness • Understand how communication channels are selected and assessed • Explore innovative communication technologies, including Generative AI applications • Develop communication skills for engaging governmental and non-governmental stakeholders • Gain exposure to public health emergency communication approaches when opportunities arise Eligibility Criteria Applicants must: • Be a U.S. Citizen or Lawful Permanent Resident (LPR) • Hold a Bachelor s or Master s degree in Public Health, Communication, or a related field • Have received their degree within the past five years (60 months) • Demonstrate interest in communication science, public health communication, or audience research • Meet all ORISE program participation requirements Important Note Applicants who have previously been employed directly by CDC or by contractors working directly for CDC are generally not eligible to participate in the ORISE program unless specific exceptions apply. Required Application Materials A complete application must include: • Online application form • Academic transcripts • Current resume or curriculum vitae (CV) • One educational or professional recommendation letter All documents must be submitted in English or accompanied by an official English translation. Appointment Details • Anticipated Start Date: August 10, 2026 • Appointment Duration: One year initially, with potential renewal • Participation Level: Full-time • Location: Atlanta, Georgia • Application Review: Rolling basis Eligible Applicants U.S. Citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents How to Apply Interested applicants should submit their applications through the ORISE online application system before the deadline. Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible since applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis throughout the recruitment period. Application Deadline September 25, 2026 Why You Should Apply This fellowship offers an exceptional opportunity for recent graduates to gain practical experience in public health communication at one of the world s leading public health agencies. Participants will learn how research informs communication strategies, develop valuable analytical and professional skills, and contribute to efforts that help protect and improve public health outcomes across the United States. Whether your interests lie in audience research, health communication, data analysis, or public health messaging, the CDC Campaign and Audience Research Team Fellowship provides a strong foundation for a future career in public health and communication science. Conclusion If you graduated within the last five years and are interested in public health communication, this fellowship could be a valuable steppingstone toward a rewarding career in health communication research and public service. With hands-on training, mentorship, and exposure to real-world public health challenges, fellows will gain experience that can help shape the next generation of communication professionals. title: PhD Opportunities in Community Ecology (Marine and Coastal Systems) at the University of Melbourne, Australia
summary: Are you passionate about understanding how biodiversity is shaped across natural ecosystems? The University of Melbourne is inviting expressions of interest from motivated students seeking to pursue a PhD in Community Ecology, Spatial Ecology, and Marine Systems under the supervision of Dr. Lynette Loke in the School of BioSciences. This exciting opportunity offers aspiring researchers the chance to contribute to innovative ecological research examining how habitat structure, dispersal, and species interactions influence biodiversity, particularly within coastal and intertidal ecosystems. Expressions of interest are being reviewed on a rolling basis, and early contact is strongly encouraged ahead of the 1 October 2026 scholarship application deadline . About the Research Dr. Lynette Loke’s research group focuses on uncovering the ecological processes that govern community assembly and biodiversity patterns across space. The lab combines field-based experimentation, quantitative data analysis, ecological modelling, and theoretical approaches to better understand how ecological communities are structured and how these patterns can be predicted. The broader research program integrates empirical ecological data with ecological theory and modelling, with much of the work conducted in coastal and intertidal environments. Research Areas Include Successful PhD candidates may work on projects involving: Designing and implementing field-based ecological studies in coastal and intertidal systems. Investigating how habitat structure influences biodiversity and species interactions. Analysing ecological data using quantitative and statistical approaches. Developing explanations for observed biodiversity patterns. Linking empirical findings with ecological theory. Applying community ecology insights to real-world environmental challenges where appropriate. Why Apply? This PhD opportunity provides students with the chance to: Conduct impactful research in marine and coastal ecosystems. Work at one of Australia’s leading research-intensive universities. Develop advanced fieldwork, analytical, and modelling skills. Contribute to fundamental ecological theory and biodiversity science. Collaborate within a vibrant academic environment focused on innovation and scientific discovery. Pursue independent research interests while receiving expert supervision. Who Can Apply? Dr. Loke is particularly interested in working with students who: Have a background in ecology, environmental science, biology, or a related discipline. Are comfortable working with ecological data and quantitative methods, including statistical analysis and software such as R. Have an interest in connecting empirical observations with ecological theory. Are willing to undertake fieldwork in coastal and intertidal environments. Are motivated to develop and pursue their own research questions. Prior experience in marine ecology is welcomed but is not a requirement. Application Requirements Interested applicants should submit the following documents: 1. Research Interest Statement A brief statement outlining: Research interests. Relevant academic or professional experience. Contact information for two referees (one should be a previous research supervisor). 2. Curriculum Vitae (CV) Including: Academic background. Relevant research experience. Academic transcripts or equivalent academic results. Both documents should be submitted as separate PDF files. How to Apply Applications and enquiries should be sent directly to: Dr. Lynette Loke 📧 lynette.loke@unimelb.edu.au Candidates are encouraged to make contact early, as expressions of interest will be considered on a rolling basis and selected applicants may be invited to an informal discussion before formal scholarship applications. For more details, visit the website HERE . Scholarship Deadline 📅 University of Melbourne Scholarship Application Deadline: 1 October 2026 Early engagement with the supervisor is highly recommended to strengthen potential scholarship applications. About the Host Institution The research will be conducted within the Spatial Community Ecology Lab at the School of BioSciences, Faculty of Science, University of Melbourne , one of Australia’s leading universities renowned for excellence in environmental and ecological research. Researchers in the lab work on fundamental questions relating to biodiversity, community assembly, spatial ecology, and ecosystem functioning, helping generate knowledge that supports conservation and environmental management efforts worldwide. Final Thoughts For students interested in biodiversity science, marine ecology, spatial ecology, and quantitative ecological research, this PhD opportunity at the University of Melbourne offers an outstanding platform to develop advanced research skills while contributing to important scientific questions about how ecological communities are formed and maintained. If you are eager to combine fieldwork, data analysis, and ecological theory in a supportive research environment, this could be the perfect opportunity to launch your research career. title: United Nations University Innovation and Education Programme Internship 2026–2027 in Japan: Paid UN Internship on AI, Sustainability, and Higher Education
summary: Are you a student or recent graduate interested in artificial intelligence, education, sustainability, international development, or public policy ? The United Nations University (UNU) is now accepting applications for its Innovation and Education (IVE) Programme Internship 2026–2027 , an exciting opportunity to work at the United Nations University Institute for the Advanced Study of Sustainability (UNU-IAS) in Tokyo, Japan . This full-time internship provides aspiring professionals with the opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge international initiatives at the intersection of AI, sustainable development, higher education, and United Nations policy . Interns will gain practical experience supporting international research networks, organizing global events, producing knowledge products, and contributing to projects that advance the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The internship runs from 15 September 2026 to 15 March 2027 (tentative) and includes a monthly stipend for eligible interns who are not receiving financial support from another source. Applications close on 7 September 2026 (11:59 PM JST). About the United Nations University (UNU) The United Nations University (UNU) is the academic and research arm of the United Nations. Established more than fifty years ago, UNU serves as: A global think tank A postgraduate teaching organization A research institution within the United Nations System UNU conducts policy-oriented research, capacity development, and knowledge dissemination that supports the goals and principles of the United Nations. Its work contributes to solving some of the world s most pressing challenges, including: Sustainable development Human security Economic development Climate change Education Peacebuilding Innovation Global governance Today, UNU operates research institutes in 12 countries , with experts working across all 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The organization collaborates closely with: United Nations agencies Governments Universities Research institutions International organizations Development partners About UNU-IAS The internship is hosted by the United Nations University Institute for the Advanced Study of Sustainability (UNU-IAS) . Based at UNU Headquarters in Tokyo, UNU-IAS is one of the thirteen research institutes within the UNU system. Its mission is to advance sustainability through: Policy-relevant research Capacity development Interdisciplinary education International collaboration Research focuses on the: Environmental dimensions of sustainability Economic dimensions of sustainability Social dimensions of sustainability UNU-IAS also develops future international leaders through postgraduate education and partnerships with scholars and professionals worldwide, particularly across Africa and Asia . About the Innovation and Education (IVE) Programme The Innovation and Education (IVE) Programme promotes research and practical approaches to: Innovative education Inclusive education Lifelong learning Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) The programme supports implementation of: UNESCO s Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) for 2030 Roadmap Greening Education Partnership Evidence-based education policy Its goal is to help translate global education priorities into meaningful local action. About the Internship Project The selected intern will support a newly established initiative: Futures of Higher Education and AI The internship contributes to the work of the new UN Higher Education Sustainability Initiative (HESI) Action Group , titled: Futures of Higher Education and AI. The Action Group brings together AI experts from higher education institutions around the world. Its objective is to strengthen global understanding of how artificial intelligence can accelerate sustainable development. Core Areas of the Project The Action Group focuses on four major themes: 1. AI in Research and Development Exploring how AI supports: Scientific research Innovation Knowledge creation 2. AI in Teaching and Learning Examining AI applications in: Learning environments Teaching methods Curriculum development Student engagement 3. AI in University Management Studying AI s role in: Administration Institutional management Operational efficiency 4. AI Ethics, Safety and Inclusion Addressing important issues including: Responsible AI Human-centred AI Ethics Inclusivity Safety Global South perspectives Women in AI Collaboration with Higher Education Networks The project also strengthens collaboration with two important higher education networks coordinated by UNU-IAS. These include: ProSPER.Net A regional Asia-Pacific network promoting sustainability in postgraduate education. SDG-University Platform (SDG-UP) A Japanese higher education network advancing the Sustainable Development Goals through education. Together with HESI, these networks contribute to knowledge sharing and international collaboration. Knowledge Products Developed Throughout the internship, the project develops numerous knowledge products, including: Podcast episodes International webinars Publications Capacity-building activities Policy dialogues United Nations event sessions These outputs emphasize: AI Sustainable development Higher education Human-centred AI Global South perspectives Women s leadership in AI Internship Responsibilities The intern works under the supervision of the Academic Programme Officer. Major responsibilities include: 1. Supporting International Higher Education Networks The intern will assist with coordination across: HESI ProSPER.Net SDG-UP Responsibilities include: Scheduling meetings Attending meetings Preparing meeting minutes Monitoring communications Following up on action points 2. Supporting International Events Interns assist in organizing: Webinars Workshops Conferences Tasks include: Preparing materials Coordinating participants Drafting event reports Supporting logistics 3. Producing Knowledge Products The intern helps produce: Podcasts Webinar content Educational resources Responsibilities include: Identifying speakers Communicating with experts Promotion Recording sessions Editing content Dissemination 4. Supporting Project Reporting Interns contribute by: Drafting project reports Documenting activities Recording outputs Maintaining organized project files 5. Other Assigned Duties Additional responsibilities may be assigned by the supervisor. Required Competencies UNU seeks candidates who embody United Nations values. Core Values Applicants should demonstrate: Inclusion Integrity Humility Humanity Expected Behaviours Successful candidates should be able to: Collaborate effectively Analyse information Plan strategically Deliver quality results Learn continuously Adapt to change Innovate creatively Eligibility Requirements Applicants should meet the following educational requirements. Education Candidates should study one of the following fields: Artificial Intelligence Information Technology Education Sustainable Development International Development Related disciplines Applicants must also: Be in the final year of an undergraduate degree, or Be enrolled in a graduate programme, or Have graduated within the previous two years from: Bachelor s degree Master s degree PhD programme Desired Skills Ideal applicants should possess: Excellent research skills Strong analytical abilities High-quality writing skills Organizational skills Event coordination experience Communication skills Experience drafting newsletters Social media content development Event summaries Outreach materials Applicants should also have familiarity with tools such as: Canva Adobe Suite Similar design and content creation platforms Language Requirements Applicants must demonstrate: Excellent written English Excellent spoken English Knowledge of another UN language, including Japanese , is considered an advantage. Internship Duration Tentative internship period: 15 September 2026 – 15 March 2027 Expected starting date: September 2026 Working Arrangements This internship is: Full-time 35 hours per week On-site Based at UNU-IAS Headquarters Location: Shibuya, Tokyo, Japan Financial Support Eligible interns receive a monthly stipend from UNU. The stipend is intended to help subsidize: Basic living expenses Important notes: The amount varies according to duty station. Interns receiving financial support from another organization may not be eligible. Stipends are paid monthly. How to Apply Applicants should submit their application through the official UNU recruitment portal. The application includes: Online application. UNU P11 Form . Motivation statement (within the P11 form). Position-specific questions. Candidates invited to interview must provide: Transcript, or Proof of enrolment or educational status. Start Your Application HERE! Selection Process Qualified applicants may undergo: Desk review Competency-based interview Background checks Reference checks You may wish to refer to the UN Values and Behaviours Framework for more information. Important Dates Activity Date Expected Start September 2026 Internship Period 15 September 2026 – 15 March 2027 (tentative) Application Deadline 7 September 2026 (11:59 PM JST) Special Notes Applicants should note the following: UNU does not sponsor work visas for this internship. Interns are not considered international civil servants . Interns are not staff members under the UN Staff Rules. UNU strongly encourages applications from: Women Persons with disabilities Candidates from developing countries Applicants of all nationalities and backgrounds UNU maintains a zero-tolerance policy regarding: Sexual harassment Exploitation Abuse Discrimination Abuse of authority Applicants should also be aware that UNU never charges application or recruitment fees . Any request for payment should be treated as fraudulent. Why You Should Apply The Innovation and Education Programme Internship offers an outstanding opportunity for students and recent graduates to gain first-hand experience within the United Nations system while contributing to globally significant work on artificial intelligence, education, sustainability, and higher education. Interns will collaborate with international experts, contribute to policy-relevant research, help organize high-level events, produce knowledge products, and strengthen their professional skills in an international, multicultural environment. For aspiring professionals interested in AI, sustainable development, education policy, or international cooperation, this internship provides valuable exposure to the work of the United Nations while building experience that can support future careers in global development, research, education, and international organizations. Visit HERE to learn more about the United Nations University Innovation and Education Programme Internship. Conclusion The United Nations University Innovation and Education Programme Internship 2026–2027 is an exceptional opportunity for students and recent graduates seeking meaningful experience in the United Nations system. Based at UNU-IAS in Tokyo, the internship places participants at the forefront of global discussions on artificial intelligence, sustainability, and higher education. Through involvement in international research networks, policy dialogues, webinars, podcasts, publications, and capacity-building initiatives, interns will gain practical skills while contributing to projects aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals. Combined with a monthly stipend for eligible interns, hands-on responsibilities, and exposure to a global network of researchers and policymakers, this internship offers a strong foundation for those aspiring to careers in international development, education, sustainability, or AI governance. Interested candidates should prepare their application materials early and submit their application before the 7 September 2026 (11:59 PM JST) deadline. title: Youth-ID Network of Multipliers 2026: Join the Erasmus+ Programme Empowering Youth Workers to Build Inclusive Communities Across Europe
summary: Youth workers play a critical role in shaping stronger, more inclusive communities by helping young people develop leadership skills, participate in civic life, and influence public decision-making. To strengthen this role, the Youth-ID – Youth Inclusive Design project is inviting passionate youth workers and professionals to become part of its Youth-ID Network of Multipliers . Funded under the Erasmus+ Programme , Youth-ID is a European initiative designed to empower young people to actively participate in designing youth-friendly and inclusive communities. Through a comprehensive 12-month programme, selected Multipliers will receive expert training, mentor young people, facilitate national seminars, participate in international mobility activities, and contribute to policy advocacy across Europe. If you are committed to youth participation, inclusive community planning, and strengthening local democracy, this opportunity offers an excellent platform to develop your professional skills while creating lasting social impact. About the Youth-ID Project Youth-ID is an Erasmus+ project focused on creating more inclusive communities by equipping young people with the knowledge, tools, and confidence needed to participate in local decision-making processes. Rather than simply involving young people in discussions, the programme enables them to become active contributors to designing public spaces, influencing local policies, and developing innovative community solutions. To achieve this goal, Youth-ID works closely with experienced youth workers, who serve as Multipliers , supporting young participants throughout the learning journey. The project combines: Inclusive design principles Participatory planning Community engagement Youth leadership Policy advocacy International collaboration Through these activities, participants contribute to building communities that better reflect the needs and voices of young people. What is the Youth-ID Network of Multipliers? The Youth-ID Network of Multipliers is a group of trained youth workers and professionals responsible for guiding young participants through the project s learning activities. Multipliers receive professional development opportunities while mentoring local youth groups, facilitating workshops, and supporting community-based initiatives throughout the project. The programme lasts 12 months , allowing participants to build long-term relationships with young people while developing practical expertise in inclusive design and civic participation. Your 12-Month Journey as a Youth-ID Multiplier Successful applicants will take part in a structured programme consisting of several key stages. 1. Expert Training in Strasbourg, France The journey begins with a two-day international training programme in Strasbourg, France . During this training, participants will: Learn participatory design methodologies. Understand intersectionality and inclusive planning. Build facilitation and mentoring skills. Connect with professionals from across Europe. Prepare to support youth-led community initiatives. This training provides the foundation needed to guide young participants throughout the programme. 2. National Scaling Activities After completing the international training, Multipliers will help organize and facilitate 12–15 hour national seminars in their home countries. These seminars aim to: Share Youth-ID methodologies. Train fellow youth professionals. Promote inclusive youth participation. Expand the project s impact nationally. Eligible countries include: Belgium France Italy Poland Cyprus North Macedonia 3. Mentoring Young People One of the most important responsibilities involves mentoring a local group of 10–15 young participants . Youth workers will guide them through practical learning activities including: Community Mapping simulations. Participatory Budgeting exercises. Local problem identification. Collaborative solution development. The mentoring process encourages youth to become active contributors within their own communities. 4. Design Labs Participants will support young people as they transform ideas into practical community initiatives. Activities include: Designing community improvement projects. Developing prototypes. Drafting local policy recommendations. Creating policy briefs for local authorities. Applying inclusive planning principles. These Design Labs help bridge the gap between youth ideas and practical implementation. 5. International Mobility Opportunities Youth-ID also includes valuable international experiences. Multipliers will accompany youth representatives during: A three-day Youth Exchange in Poland . The EU Advocacy Marathon in Brussels . These mobility activities provide opportunities to: Exchange ideas with international peers. Learn from different community approaches. Strengthen European collaboration. Expand professional networks. Promote intercultural learning. 6. Showcasing Community Impact Towards the end of the programme, participants will showcase the achievements of their local youth groups through: Local Showcase events. A Transnational Online Fair. These events provide an opportunity to celebrate youth-led innovation while sharing successful community projects with a wider European audience. Benefits of Joining the Youth-ID Network Selected Multipliers will enjoy numerous professional and personal development opportunities throughout the programme. These include: International Mobility Participants will travel to various European activities, including: Strasbourg, France Poland Brussels, Belgium These experiences encourage international networking and knowledge exchange. Professional Training The programme provides expert-led training covering: Inclusive community planning Participatory design Youth engagement Facilitation skills Policy advocacy YouthPass Certification Upon completing the programme, participants will receive a YouthPass Certificate , formally recognizing the competencies and skills gained during the Erasmus+ project. Access to Learning Resources Multipliers receive access to: The Youth-ID Digital Handbook European collaboration platforms Educational resources Practical mentoring tools These resources remain valuable beyond the duration of the project. Real Community Impact Participants directly contribute to: More inclusive public spaces Stronger youth participation Better local policymaking Community-led innovation Youth empowerment The programme enables professionals to create lasting change within their local communities. Who Should Apply? Youth-ID is seeking motivated professionals who are passionate about empowering young people and promoting inclusive development. Applicants should be: Active youth workers. Professionals working within youth organisations. Individuals committed to European values. Supporters of inclusive community planning. Willing to mentor young people over a 12-month period. Available to participate in all required project activities. AAPLY HERE Successful applicants should demonstrate enthusiasm for collaboration, learning, and youth participation. Why This Programme Matters Young people remain among the most important drivers of social innovation, yet they often have limited opportunities to influence decisions affecting their communities. Youth-ID addresses this challenge by equipping youth workers with practical tools that enable meaningful youth participation. The project promotes: Democratic engagement Social inclusion Community resilience Youth leadership Cross-border collaboration Sustainable local development By investing in youth workers, Youth-ID creates ripple effects that benefit entire communities across Europe. Why You Should Apply Joining the Youth-ID Network of Multipliers provides an opportunity to: Develop advanced professional skills. Gain international experience. Travel across Europe. Build lasting professional networks. Mentor the next generation of community leaders. Influence local policies. Promote inclusive public participation. Strengthen your career through Erasmus+ recognition. Whether you already work with young people or are looking to deepen your impact in youth development, this programme offers practical experience combined with international collaboration. How to Apply Interested youth workers should submit their expression of interest through the official Youth-ID application platform. Applicants are encouraged to carefully review all programme requirements and ensure they are available to participate throughout the full 12-month implementation period. Visit HERE to learn more about the Youth-ID Network of Multipliers 2026 Application Deadline No application deadline has been provided in the information available. Interested applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible once the official call is open. Conclusion The Youth-ID Network of Multipliers is an outstanding opportunity for youth workers who want to strengthen their professional skills while empowering young people to shape more inclusive communities. Through expert training, international mobility, mentoring opportunities, and policy engagement, participants become part of a growing European movement committed to youth participation and community transformation. If you are passionate about youth empowerment, inclusive design, and creating meaningful social impact, this Erasmus+ initiative offers the knowledge, international exposure, and practical experience needed to help young people become active architects of their communities. For more global grants, scholarships, fellowships, internships, jobs, conferences, competitions, and other career opportunities for young people, visit the Opportunities for Youth (OFY) website at www.opportunitiesforyouth.org.
